uncited: Gaussian Splatting SLAM is a simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) method that reconstructs a scene as a collection of 3D Gaussians while estimating camera poses, building on [3D Gaussian Splatting Optimization](15143-3d-gaussian-splatting-optimization.md).
- **Inputs:** Current camera pose $T_{CW}$, current Gaussian set $\mathcal{G}$, incoming RGB-D frame (color image $I$, depth map $D$).
- **Gaussians ($\mathcal{G}$):** Each Gaussian $g$ has position $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, scale $\mathbf{s}$, rotation $\mathbf{q}$, color $\mathbf{c}$, opacity $\alpha$.
**Tracking:** Estimate the current camera pose $T_{CW}$ by minimizing the loss function below.
**Mapping:** Update the Gaussian parameters and keyframe poses.
- Minimize the mapping loss over all Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$ and keyframes $k \in \mathcal{W}$.
**Keyframing:** Select new keyframes based on Gaussian covisibility.
It extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to SLAM by integrating tracking and mapping modules that optimize both camera poses and Gaussian parameters simultaneously.
